data.text: Your book says: "Snakes coil around their eggs to keep them warm." More exactly: some snakes, such as pythons, coil around their eggs. Many other snakes lay their eggs and leave them. Use your book's words in class and tests. You can also show this note to your teacher.
Is a hen living or non-living? How do you know?
data.answer: Living. A hen eats, breathes, grows, moves and has young ones. Not sure? Read the note on non-living things in "The human life cycle".

data.text: Which of these animals gives birth to young ones?
Explain to someone at home how a tadpole becomes a frog.
data.answer: Eggs in water hatch into tadpoles, which breathe with gills; they grow legs, lose their tails, and become frogs that breathe with lungs.

data.text: Imagine you are inside a chrysalis. What would you feel?
data.answer: There is no single right answer. Think about the dark, the quiet and the change happening to your body.

data.text: Under the hood, `markForCheck()` marks the component and its ancestors dirty up to the root, so the next tick visits them.
In one breath: an OnPush component is checked only when an input reference, its own event, a signal it reads or an async pipe changes.

Immutable update. Intent: give OnPush a new reference. Use when: changing a list or object held in a signal or input. Smell: mutating in place and calling set with the same object. Avoid when: the data is never shown by an OnPush component.

concept.text: Young ones are the same kind of animal as their parents.

challenges.given: A duck lays eggs, just like a hen.
challenges.thinkAbout: Never seen a duck up close? Think about ducks you've seen in pictures or on TV.
challenges.ask: We learned that chicks hatch from a hen's eggs. What would you expect to hatch from a duck's egg?

options.text: A young duck
options.fb: Yes. Living things produce young ones of their own kind, so a duck's egg hatches into a young duck.

options.text: A chick
options.fb: A chick is a hen's young one. Living things produce young ones of their own kind, so a duck's egg hatches into a young duck.

options.text: It could be any kind of bird
options.fb: Living things always produce young ones of their own kind, so a duck's egg hatches into a young duck, not any other bird.

challenges.hint: Remember the cat and the chicks: what kind of young ones does an animal have?
challenges.idea: Living things produce young ones of their own kind.

explain.speaker: tara
explain.text: A young duck is called a duckling. It's the same kind of animal as its parent.

followUp.given: A duckling is covered in soft, fluffy feathers that are often yellow or brown. Many grown ducks have smooth feathers of other colours.
followUp.ask: So a duckling doesn't look exactly like its parent. Is it still a duck?

options.text: Yes. It's a duck's offspring, so it's a duck, even if it looks different for now.
options.fb: Yes. Like the grey-brown cygnet and the white swan, offspring can look different from their parents at first and still be the same kind of animal.

options.text: No. It looks different, so it must be a different animal.
options.fb: Looking different doesn't make it a different animal. The cygnet is grey-brown and the swan is white, but the cygnet is still a swan. In the same way, a duckling is still a duck.

followUp.hint: Remember the cygnet and the swan.
followUp.idea: Living things produce young ones of their own kind.

explain.speaker: kavi
explain.text: Same as the cygnet: it can look different at first and still be the same kind of animal as its parent.

sections.title: The butterfly: a complete change

lines.speaker: kavi
lines.text: Is this caterpillar really the same animal as this butterfly? They look completely different.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: That's the question for this page. The butterfly is another animal whose young one doesn't look like the adult.

book.text: Another animal whose life cycle includes stages in which the young one does not look like the adult is the butterfly.
The young caterpillar does not look like the adult butterfly.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: We've seen two stages. The next card is hidden.

act.ask: The caterpillar has eaten enough. What do you think happens next?

options.text: It turns into a butterfly straight away.
options.fb: Not yet. There's one more stage before the butterfly: the caterpillar attaches itself under a leaf or twig and makes a hard covering. It becomes a pupa.

options.text: It attaches itself under a leaf or twig and makes a hard covering.
options.fb: Yes. It attaches itself under a leaf or twig and makes a hard covering. Now it's called a pupa.

options.text: It lays eggs.
options.fb: Laying eggs is what the adult butterfly does at the start of the cycle, and the caterpillar isn't an adult yet. Next, it attaches itself under a leaf or twig and makes a hard covering: it becomes a pupa.

act.hint: There are four cards in the circle, and we've only seen two.
act.idea: After eating enough, the caterpillar attaches itself under a leaf or twig and makes a hard covering, the chrysalis. It is now a pupa.

explain.speaker: tara
explain.text: It attaches itself under a leaf or a twig. Now it's called a pupa.

explain.speaker: kavi
explain.text: And it makes a hard, smooth, shiny covering around itself, called the chrysalis.

book.text: When the caterpillar has eaten enough, it attaches itself under a leaf or a twig. It is now called a pupa. It makes a hard, smooth, shiny covering around itself, called the chrysalis. Inside, it slowly changes to become an adult butterfly.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: Let's see if we can rebuild the whole cycle without looking at the notes.

act.ask: Put the four stages in order, starting from the eggs.
act.start: Start from the eggs: the first card the arrows begin at.
act.hint: Follow the arrows around the circle.

explain.speaker: kavi
explain.text: Eggs, caterpillar, pupa, adult butterfly. Then the adult lays eggs, and the cycle starts again.

book.text: Butterfly: eggs → larva (caterpillar) → pupa (chrysalis) → adult butterfly.

items: What is metamorphosis?
The series of physical changes that an animal goes through in the different stages of its life cycle, like a caterpillar becoming a butterfly.
What is the larva of a butterfly called?
A caterpillar.
What is the difference between a chrysalis and a cocoon?
A chrysalis is the hard covering of a butterfly's pupa. A cocoon is the soft silk case that a moth's caterpillar spins around itself.

Metamorphosis is the series of physical changes an animal goes through in its life cycle. Butterflies and frogs both go through it.

concept.text: Metamorphosis means big changes in body form as an animal grows.

challenges.given: A kitten looks like a small cat when it's born. A tadpole lives in water, has a tail and no legs at first, and grows into a frog.
challenges.thinkAbout: Think about kittens and tadpoles you've seen, or picture them.
challenges.ask: Which young one changes its body form a lot as it grows, like the caterpillar does?

options.text: The tadpole
options.fb: Yes. A tadpole looks very different from a frog and changes a lot as it grows. That's metamorphosis, like the caterpillar becoming a butterfly.

options.text: The kitten
options.fb: A kitten already looks like a small cat; it mostly grows bigger. The tadpole is the one whose body form changes a lot, and that's metamorphosis.

options.text: Both change in the same way
options.fb: They both grow, but differently. A kitten mostly grows bigger, while a tadpole's body form changes a lot. That big change is metamorphosis.

challenges.hint: Which young one looks least like its parent?
challenges.idea: Some animals, like butterflies and frogs, go through big changes in body form as they grow. That is metamorphosis.

explain.speaker: tara
explain.text: The frog goes through metamorphosis too, just like the butterfly. The kitten simply grows.

the process by which living things produce young ones of their own kind.
Offspring
the young one of an animal.

book.text: Reproduction is the process by which living things produce young ones of their own kind. The young one of an animal is also known as its offspring.

lines.text: Tara wrote our summary. I think one line needs fixing. Can you find it?

lines: Reproduction is the process by which living things produce young ones of their own kind.
The young one of an animal is its offspring.

act.findHint: Look for the line that says why living things reproduce.
act.fixAsk: How should that line say it?

fixes.text: Living things reproduce to continue their existence on Earth.
fixes.fb: Yes. That's the reason the book gives.

fixes.text: Living things reproduce so that they can live longer.
fixes.fb: Reproducing doesn't make an animal live longer. It makes young ones, which keep their kind going on Earth.

explain.speaker: tara
explain.text: I mixed up growing and reproducing. Growing makes one animal bigger. Reproducing makes new young ones.

book.text: Reproduction is the process by which living things produce young ones of their own kind.
The young one of an animal is its offspring.
Living things reproduce to continue their existence on Earth.

summary: Reproduction is the process by which living things produce young ones of their own kind.
The young one of an animal is its offspring.

concept.text: Young ones are the same kind of animal as their parents.

challenges.given: A duck lays eggs, just like a hen.
challenges.thinkAbout: Never seen a duck up close? Think about ducks you've seen in pictures or on TV.
challenges.ask: We learned that chicks hatch from a hen's eggs. What would you expect to hatch from a duck's egg?

options.text: A young duck
options.fb: Yes. Living things produce young ones of their own kind, so a duck's egg hatches into a young duck.

options.text: A chick
options.fb: A chick is a hen's young one. Living things produce young ones of their own kind, so a duck's egg hatches into a young duck.

options.text: It could be any kind of bird
options.fb: Living things always produce young ones of their own kind, so a duck's egg hatches into a young duck, not any other bird.

challenges.hint: Remember the cat and the chicks: what kind of young ones does an animal have?
challenges.idea: Living things produce young ones of their own kind.

explain.speaker: tara
explain.text: A young duck is called a duckling. It's the same kind of animal as its parent.

followUp.given: A duckling is covered in soft, fluffy feathers that are often yellow or brown. Many grown ducks have smooth feathers of other colours.
followUp.ask: So a duckling doesn't look exactly like its parent. Is it still a duck?

options.text: Yes. It's a duck's offspring, so it's a duck, even if it looks different for now.
options.fb: Yes. Like the grey-brown cygnet and the white swan, offspring can look different from their parents at first and still be the same kind of animal.

options.text: No. It looks different, so it must be a different animal.
options.fb: Looking different doesn't make it a different animal. The cygnet is grey-brown and the swan is white, but the cygnet is still a swan. In the same way, a duckling is still a duck.

followUp.hint: Remember the cygnet and the swan.
followUp.idea: Living things produce young ones of their own kind.

explain.speaker: kavi
explain.text: Same as the cygnet: it can look different at first and still be the same kind of animal as its parent.

sections.title: The butterfly: a complete change

lines.speaker: kavi
lines.text: Is this caterpillar really the same animal as this butterfly? They look completely different.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: That's the question for this page. The butterfly is another animal whose young one doesn't look like the adult.

book.text: Another animal whose life cycle includes stages in which the young one does not look like the adult is the butterfly.
The young caterpillar does not look like the adult butterfly.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: We've seen two stages. The next card is hidden.

act.ask: The caterpillar has eaten enough. What do you think happens next?

options.text: It turns into a butterfly straight away.
options.fb: Not yet. There's one more stage before the butterfly: the caterpillar attaches itself under a leaf or twig and makes a hard covering. It becomes a pupa.

options.text: It attaches itself under a leaf or twig and makes a hard covering.
options.fb: Yes. It attaches itself under a leaf or twig and makes a hard covering. Now it's called a pupa.

options.text: It lays eggs.
options.fb: Laying eggs is what the adult butterfly does at the start of the cycle, and the caterpillar isn't an adult yet. Next, it attaches itself under a leaf or twig and makes a hard covering: it becomes a pupa.

act.hint: There are four cards in the circle, and we've only seen two.
act.idea: After eating enough, the caterpillar attaches itself under a leaf or twig and makes a hard covering, the chrysalis. It is now a pupa.

explain.speaker: tara
explain.text: It attaches itself under a leaf or a twig. Now it's called a pupa.

explain.speaker: kavi
explain.text: And it makes a hard, smooth, shiny covering around itself, called the chrysalis.

book.text: When the caterpillar has eaten enough, it attaches itself under a leaf or a twig. It is now called a pupa. It makes a hard, smooth, shiny covering around itself, called the chrysalis. Inside, it slowly changes to become an adult butterfly.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: Let's see if we can rebuild the whole cycle without looking at the notes.

act.ask: Put the four stages in order, starting from the eggs.
act.start: Start from the eggs: the first card the arrows begin at.
act.hint: Follow the arrows around the circle.

explain.speaker: kavi
explain.text: Eggs, caterpillar, pupa, adult butterfly. Then the adult lays eggs, and the cycle starts again.

book.text: Butterfly: eggs → larva (caterpillar) → pupa (chrysalis) → adult butterfly.

items: What is metamorphosis?
The series of physical changes that an animal goes through in the different stages of its life cycle, like a caterpillar becoming a butterfly.
What is the larva of a butterfly called?
A caterpillar.
What is the difference between a chrysalis and a cocoon?
A chrysalis is the hard covering of a butterfly's pupa. A cocoon is the soft silk case that a moth's caterpillar spins around itself.

book.text: What is metamorphosis? The series of physical changes that an animal goes through in the different stages of its life cycle, like a caterpillar becoming a butterfly.
What is the larva of a butterfly called? A caterpillar.
What is the difference between a chrysalis and a cocoon? A chrysalis is the hard covering of a butterfly's pupa. A cocoon is the soft silk case that a moth's caterpillar spins around itself.

lines.speaker: kavi
lines.text: Now explain it to Tara, out loud. She wants to check her own notes against yours.

act.ask: Tell Tara the four stages of a butterfly's life cycle, in order, and what happens in each.
checks: eggs laid on a leaf
the caterpillar (larva) eats a lot and sheds its skin
the pupa inside a hard chrysalis, changing inside
the adult butterfly breaks out and flies away
the word metamorphosis

after.speaker: tara
after.text: Let's both check our notes against the same list. Anything missing is worth another look.

book.text: Teach it back. Tell your parent the four stages of a butterfly's life cycle, in order, and what happens in each.

summary: Butterfly: eggs → larva (caterpillar) → pupa (chrysalis) → adult butterfly.
The young caterpillar does not look like the adult butterfly.
Metamorphosis is the series of physical changes an animal goes through in its life cycle. Butterflies and frogs both go through it.

concept.text: Metamorphosis means big changes in body form as an animal grows.

challenges.given: A kitten looks like a small cat when it's born. A tadpole lives in water, has a tail and no legs at first, and grows into a frog.
challenges.thinkAbout: Think about kittens and tadpoles you've seen, or picture them.
challenges.ask: Which young one changes its body form a lot as it grows, like the caterpillar does?

options.text: The tadpole
options.fb: Yes. A tadpole looks very different from a frog and changes a lot as it grows. That's metamorphosis, like the caterpillar becoming a butterfly.

options.text: The kitten
options.fb: A kitten already looks like a small cat; it mostly grows bigger. The tadpole is the one whose body form changes a lot, and that's metamorphosis.

options.text: Both change in the same way
options.fb: They both grow, but differently. A kitten mostly grows bigger, while a tadpole's body form changes a lot. That big change is metamorphosis.

challenges.hint: Which young one looks least like its parent?
challenges.idea: Some animals, like butterflies and frogs, go through big changes in body form as they grow. That is metamorphosis.

explain.speaker: tara
explain.text: The frog goes through metamorphosis too, just like the butterfly. The kitten simply grows.
